name: Ammonia compression refrigeration
summary: Mechanical refrigeration that uses ammonia as the working fluid in a vapor-compression cycle.

name: Apochromatic microscope objective
summary: A microscope objective corrected so that three colours of light come to a common focus, greatly reducing colour fringing.

name: Aquaculture
summary: Raising and managing fish or other aquatic animals in enclosed or controlled waters.

name: Aqueduct
summary: A built channel that carries water by gravity over long distances to supply a settlement or works.

name: Atmospheric steam engine
summary: An engine in which condensing steam under a piston creates a vacuum so that air pressure drives the working stroke.

name: Boat mill
summary: A mill mounted on moored boats so a waterwheel is turned by a river's current.

name: Central electricity station
summary: A single generating plant that supplies electricity through a distribution network to many separate customers.

name: Co-fusion steelmaking
summary: Making steel by heating high-carbon cast iron together with low-carbon iron so their carbon contents even out.

name: Compound steam engine
summary: A steam engine in which steam expands successively in two or more cylinders.

name: Continuous paper machine
summary: Forming paper mechanically as an endless web on a moving wire instead of in single hand-made sheets.

name: Copper smelting
summary: Extracting copper metal from its ores by heating them with fuel, achieved in several regions.

name: Decarburized cast iron
summary: Casting iron to shape and then removing carbon by prolonged oxidising heat to make it tougher.

name: DNA sequencing
summary: Determining the order of bases in a DNA molecule.

name: Double-hulled voyaging canoe
summary: A sailing vessel of two hulls joined by a deck, used for long open-ocean voyages in the Pacific.

name: Electric motor
summary: A device that turns electric current into continuous mechanical motion through magnetic forces.

name: Electromagnetic generator
summary: A machine that turns mechanical motion into electric current by moving conductors relative to a magnetic field.

name: Electromagnetic induction
summary: The production of an electric current in a circuit by a changing magnetic field.

name: Expansive steam working
summary: Cutting off steam admission part-way through the piston stroke and letting the enclosed steam expand to finish it, saving fuel.

name: Fish trap
summary: A fixed structure of stone, wood or fibre that channels and holds fish or eels so they can be caught.

name: Fluorescent DNA sequencing
summary: Labelling sequencing products with distinguishable fluorescent dyes so the base order can be read automatically.

name: Froth flotation
summary: Separating fine mineral particles by attaching selected ones to gas bubbles that carry them to the surface of a slurry.

name: Hafir
summary: An excavated and embanked reservoir that catches seasonal runoff for storage in dry lands.

name: High-level language compiler
summary: A program that translates code written in human-oriented notation into a computer's machine instructions.

name: High-strength aramid fibre
summary: Spinning rigid aromatic polyamides into highly oriented fibres of very high strength for their weight.

name: Hindu-Arabic numeral arithmetic
summary: Calculating with nine digits and a zero written by decimal place value, passed from India through the Islamic world to Europe.

name: Hot blast
summary: Preheating the air blown into a furnace to save fuel and raise temperature.

name: Infinitesimal calculus
summary: A general method for calculating rates of change, tangents, areas and sums using infinitely small quantities or limits.

name: Integrated circuit
summary: Making a complete electronic circuit, with its components and connections, in or on a single piece of semiconductor.

name: Isotactic polypropylene
summary: Making crystalline, stereoregular polypropylene by catalytic polymerisation, achieved separately at Milan and at Phillips Petroleum in the early 1950s.

name: Logarithms
summary: Tables or scales that turn multiplication and division into addition and subtraction.

name: Long-distance electric power transmission
summary: Sending electric power over lines from a distant generating source to where it is used.

name: Magnetic tape data storage
summary: Recording digital data on moving magnetic tape for computers to write and read back in sequence.

name: Marine chronometer
summary: A portable timekeeper accurate enough at sea to find longitude by comparing local time with a reference time.

name: Mechanical equivalent of heat
summary: Establishing how much mechanical work corresponds to a given quantity of heat.

name: Meteoritic iron working
summary: Shaping iron from meteorites by cold or hot hammering, without smelting ore.

name: Mold-blown glass
summary: Shaping and decorating glass vessels by blowing hot glass into a mold.

name: Molded plastic radio cabinet
summary: A radio receiver housing formed in one piece by moulding a synthetic plastic such as Bakelite instead of building it from wood.

name: Movable-type printing
summary: Printing from individual reusable characters that are assembled into a page and then separated for reuse.

name: Multistage steam turbine
summary: A rotary steam engine that extracts energy in successive stages of fixed and moving blade rows on one shaft.

name: Native copper working
summary: Hammering and annealing naturally occurring pure copper into tools and ornaments without smelting.

name: Natural selection
summary: The explanation of adaptation through inherited variation and differential survival and reproduction.

name: Non-instrument wayfinding
summary: Navigating the open ocean by stars, swells, winds, birds and other natural cues, without compass, chart or instruments.

name: Noria
summary: A water wheel turned by a river current that lifts water in attached buckets or compartments to a higher channel.

name: Oxygen steelmaking
summary: Making steel by blowing pure oxygen onto or through molten iron to remove carbon.

name: Papermaking
summary: Forming a thin sheet by dispersing plant fibres in water and collecting them on a mould.

name: Plant domestication
summary: Turning wild plants into crops through human selection and cultivation, so that they depend on people and yield more.

name: Pneumatic steelmaking
summary: Making steel by blowing air through molten pig iron so that oxidation removes carbon and supplies heat.

name: Point-contact transistor
summary: A solid-state amplifier in which closely spaced metal point contacts on a semiconductor crystal control current flow.

name: Pressure flaking
summary: Shaping stone edges by pressing small flakes off with a pointed tool rather than striking them.

name: Public electric telegraph service
summary: An electric telegraph network whose offices accept and deliver messages for paying members of the public.

name: Pulse oximetry
summary: Estimating arterial oxygen saturation from the pulsing part of red and infrared light passing through tissue.

name: Reed boat
summary: A watercraft built from bundles of reeds such as papyrus or totora lashed together, known from ancient Egypt, Mesopotamia and the Andes.

name: Refracting telescope
summary: An instrument using lenses to make distant objects appear nearer and larger.

name: Relational query optimization
summary: Having a database system choose an efficient way to execute a declarative query among many possible plans.

name: Relay postal system
summary: A state messenger service that passes messages between stationed runners or riders at fixed posts along a route so they travel faster than one messenger could.

name: Rotative steam engine
summary: A steam engine whose reciprocating motion is converted into continuous shaft rotation to drive machinery.

name: Saqiya
summary: An animal-powered water-lifting wheel in which a turning animal drives gearing that raises water in containers.

name: Semiconductor photolithography
summary: Using light-sensitive resist exposed through a pattern to define regions on a semiconductor wafer for etching or doping.

name: Shunting outrigger sailing
summary: Reversing a sailing canoe's direction by swapping bow and stern, so a single outrigger float stays on the same side of the wind.

name: Single-chip microprocessor
summary: A complete computer central processing unit built on one integrated circuit.

name: Slit snow goggles
summary: Opaque eye shields with narrow slits that cut glare from snow and ice to prevent snow blindness.

name: Snowshoe
summary: Footwear that spreads a walker's weight over a broad frame so they can travel over soft snow.

name: Solid-state image sensor
summary: A semiconductor chip that converts a light image into electrical signals.

name: Spear-thrower
summary: A hand-held lever that launches a separate dart or spear, found among many separate peoples such as the Australian woomera and the American atlatl.

name: State road network
summary: A connected system of built roads maintained by a state to move officials, messages, troops and goods across its territory.

name: Stored-program computer
summary: An electronic computer that holds its program in the same memory as its data, so it can be changed without rewiring.

name: Time-sharing
summary: Letting many users work interactively on one computer at once by rapidly switching it between them.

name: Toggling harpoon
summary: A harpoon head that detaches on a line and turns crosswise in the wound so it cannot pull out.

name: Transatlantic telegraph cable
summary: A submarine cable across the Atlantic Ocean carrying electric telegraph signals between Europe and North America.

name: Twin-wire paper forming
summary: Draining water from a forming paper or board web through two wires so it leaves from both sides.

name: Vapor-compression refrigeration
summary: Cooling by evaporating a fluid, then compressing and condensing its vapor so the fluid can be reused in a closed loop.

name: Voltaic battery
summary: A chemical source of continuous electric current built from cells of dissimilar metals and an electrolyte.

name: Water-powered stone saw
summary: A waterwheel driving saw blades back and forth to cut stone.

name: Water-returning engine
summary: A pumping engine that lifts water from below a waterwheel back to its supply so the wheel can keep working.

name: Watermill
summary: A mill in which a water-turned wheel drives machinery such as millstones.

name: Writing
summary: A system of lasting visible signs that records language or information so that others can read it later.

name: Zero placeholder in positional numerals
summary: Writing a sign for an empty place in a positional number system, reached separately in Mesopotamia, Mesoamerica and South or Southeast Asia.
